notes.title: Crusader: DE - Update & DLC 1 Reveals
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yn98HHTPl4k
With your help [b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] has charged into the breach and emerged from its launch victorious! The response from fans has been nothing short of stellar and we're pleased to reveal some of our initial content plans in today's developer update!

While we're still working hard to add features, fixes and tweaks that players have been requesting (See our extensive [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3024040?emclan=103582791474973564&emgid=510713456384540934]v1.03 Patch Notes[/url] for the latest changes), we're keeping this momentum going by revealing new details of gameplay content players can look forward to in the coming months. With additional updates like v1.03 and more coming before then...

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/7e913c19b867710e01e146ce956448016cbc3536.png[/img]

Our first major ‘Autumn’ update will arrive in two parts, a free content update and an optional paid DLC. This will introduce The Crocodile, a brand new computer-controlled opponent with his own tactics, castle design, army and of course, snappy personality!

A wizened lord of the marshes, The Crocodile is a bitter cruel fellow, driven beyond sanity by envy of his rival lords. Players will encounter The Crocodile across a new five mission economic campaign, in addition to being playable in skirmish mode (And in case you’re wondering - Yes, the campaign has actual crocodiles too!)

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/7557f64cf23973225f79db991c093f05eb189374.png[/img]

While there will be some degree of combat to contend with in the economic campaign, the ultimate goal and thus victory will be decided by mastery of the game’s various economic industries and castle-life mechanics. The free component of the Autumn Update will be capped off by the inclusion of three new maps - One for Skirmish, Freebuild and Multiplayer.

These will release alongside our first DLC featuring two new CPU commanders in the form of The Canary and The Trader, as well as a new 9 mission ‘Sands of Time’ skirmish trail. Players can expect military scenarios will test their strategic prowess and skills of siegecraft, as they wage war against these new tricky CPU characters. Fear not, more about these new adversaries and their attributes will be revealed in due time!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/59e21472a7555da6a8e316f878fe973f43fe3f13.png[/img]

After Crusader: DE’s fantastic launch, we are determined to keep pushing further with fixes, content updates and gameplay improvements inbound, to truly make this Definitive Edition a game worthy of the Crusader name.

Thanks for playing and stay tuned for more updates coming soon!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

notes.title: Stronghold Crusader: DE - Out Now!
notes.notes:

The time is NOW, Sire! The long march is finally over and your forces have finally arrived at our divine destination - [b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] is out now with a 10% launch discount!

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/78768ab274c6e0caa0b059e9287f9ed8fbd0f1a4.jpg[/img]

The tremendous outpouring of love has pushed us to make this definitive edition of the fan-favourite Crusader the best it possible can be, adding more features, fixes and content than anyone could have expected. We can't wait to see how fans take this reimagined classic and make it their own.

Every bit of feedback across our demos has helped to inform the final game, allowing us to craft this expanded remaster hand-in-hand with the community. This player-first development focus has helped to shape this into a love letter to the golden age of isometric strategy games, one that will continue after launch with a robust roadmap of updates and DLC.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/9ab26dce854ef8398e3416cbf0c264f3769047c8.png[/img]

With improvements and expansions to practically every core feature and beyond: reworked visuals, higher fidelity audio, new units, new AI Lords, new modes, 10k units cap, co-op, new missions, larger-than-ever maps, 8-player Steam multiplayer, Steam Workshop support, QoL improvements and more!

[b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] is the culmination of almost a quarter century of development experience, fan support and technological advancements. Better-looking, smoother-running and bigger in all ways possible, Stronghold Crusader: DE is the ultimate way to take a trip down memory lane.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

Seen a bug? Got feedback? Please submit issues both large and small through the [url=https://fireflyworlds.com/support/]Firefly Studios support site[/url]. notes.title: Stronghold Crusader: DE - Roadmap Reveal
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=71UzpnLOH7U

[h1]Updates and DLC To Add New Lords, Customisation and More![/h1]

Good Day, Sire! [b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] is now less than two weeks from launch, so what better time than now to share all there is to know about the game's post-release plans!

Following the positive reception of the two public demos and in keeping with Stronghold: DE’s post-launch, we're announcing two major post-launch content updates for Crusader: DE. These will take the form of an Autumn and a Winter Update, both releasing this year alongside two paid DLCs.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/8f40990ce7a71421b643639197584c99a4027f26.png[/img]

The free initial Autumn Update will feature a series-first economic campaign as well as a brand new CPU commander. Five missions will challenge players to complete a series of economic objectives, leaning heavily into our city builder gameplay mechanics. The new computer-controlled character can meanwhile also be played as friend or foe, selectable in the game’s offline skirmish and online multiplayer modes. Last but not least, three new maps will also be added, one for skirmish, another in Free Build mode and a balanced multiplayer battlefield.

Following this content drop, the game’s free Winter Update will add perhaps the greatest player request so far... The ability to customise CPU opponents, castles and campaigns! Players will be able to create the rivals or allies of their dreams (or nightmares), design their defences and then place all of this into custom mission scenarios created by the community.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/5313cab036a111f6c5b495987e9b8564aad4fdd7.png[/img]

If that wasn’t enough, the Winter Update continues this community-first trend with the addition of a second co-op trail of missions. The 10 missions found in the first co-op trail not enough for you? Well, dare to brave the challenges of this new trail and you just might come out victorious. Once again a new map pack of three maps will be added to the overall pool, keeping things fresh for players after launch.

[b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] launches soon on July 15th. Wishlist now to be the first to know when it goes live!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

notes.title: New Coop Trailer & Next Fest
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pXejCnia8tc
Good tidings, Sire! Steam Next Fest is now live and with it our second public demo for [b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b]. Showcasing the latest fixes, a full Sands of Time mission, Historical Campaign challenge and allowing you to freely try out Custom Skirmish mode before the game’s July 15th launch, this is our most content rich demo yet! So if you haven’t yet given it a try or think you can rise even higher on the leaderboards, now is the chance to prove your mettle…

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/f31175fe2a59eb5b38fcfa0887614d2337a31aee.jpg[/img]

Crusader: DE was designed with your feedback in mind and at the very top of that list were features like a proper coop mode. In past games we have offered coop in the form of team-based skirmish play and - In the case of Stronghold Crusader 2 - The ability for two players to control the same castle. In Crusader: DE we have gone a step further and designed a full 10 mission skirmish trail, allowing two players to cooperate and defeat the AI across a selection of new maps… With one or two classic battlefields thrown in there for good measure!

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/5122089a08847a6e822d67e5ef76f327250b69d3.jpg[/img]

Featuring the game’s new AI opponents, units and more, this mode takes full advantage of everything Crusader: DE has to offer. In addition to all of this, we are pleased to announce that - Even though it's called a ‘Coop Trail’ - Solo players won’t be left out in the cold. If for whatever reason you are unable to buddy up with another human player online, the trail is fully playable with the help of one of our 20 AI characters! Battle alongside everyone from The Snake to The Sentinel, as you conquer this fresh take on classic skirmish trail gameplay.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/09b0b6d9de45258482f62b6afdf7adeafc40898b.jpg[/img]

Nothing forges stronger bonds than conquering challenges together. Whether it’s reuniting with distant pals, bonding with a new crusading comrade or finally teaming up with the Lord of Rats himself, the series-first coop mode for Stronghold Crusader: DE will be your chance to create new memories across fresh battlefields!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

notes.title: Feature Spotlight: 10k Unit Cap, Mosques & More!
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=js6TBaUA8QQ
Good morrow, my liege! After 150,000 demo downloads, three times as many as Stronghold: Definitive Edition... We have channelled thousands of your Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition feedback forms into new player-requested enhancements!

Ahead of the game's July 15th launch, today we dive into some of these community-requested features, confirming key information on maximum unit counts and more in our final ‘Feature Spotlight’ development diary.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/aec37b428c9d5d6fbc474ee8e12bf8beff52dbf5.jpg[/img]

As some of Crusader’s most knowledgeable and experienced players, your feedback on our upcoming Definitive Edition has been invaluable. So naturally suggestions and ideas discussed online were studied in close detail, ahead of the game’s reveal earlier this year. Your Crusader: DE feedback was then further examined after January 20th, using the demo’s feedback form.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/107cdacbe8c55c27bde088845cf0faedefbdf0d7.jpg[/img]

Many features have been requested by players since January. These include raising the overall troop count to a whopping 10,000 soldiers in a single game, to match that of Stronghold Crusader Extreme, which we can confirm today. We have also made the addition of a few Islamic buildings and related workers for the game’s Arabic and Bedouin Lords, as well as many vital bug fixes. The latter addresses specific exploits and issues discovered by the game’s most dedicated players across more than 20 years of play.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/3f8c87f54432ea3613e3890146d4c970d5533921.jpg[/img]

From map sizes up to four times the size of those available in the original, through to custom toggles for skirmish mode and online leader boards, we are striving to tick every possible box for fans of the original game. A Definitive Edition should include absolutely everything possible that players want out of Crusader and that’s what this final version intends to deliver!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

notes.title: Valley of the Wolf & Spring Update - Coming April 30th!

[b]Snarls[/b] Soon you will see what it means to wage real warfare! That is... In our final instalment of the [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] 'Jewel' campaign! [i]Valley of the Wolf[/i] extends the base game with seven new missions and extra achievements. Under the tutelage of the wise Sergeant, finish the fight by rescuing Sir Longarm's captured kin once and for all, when this new DLC releases for $2.99, €2.99 and £2.49 on April 30th.

This final chapter of 'The Jewel' campaign pits players against the greatest rogue of them all... The vicious Wolf! To safely retrieve the Jewel of the North and put an end to The Wolf's insidious scourge, players must plunge directly into the belly of the beast and bring the fight to his borders. Malbork, the fortress erected by the Teutonic Order to signify their Prussian conquest, Biskupin, an ancient stronghold built at the dawn of Rome, and Niedzica, a daunting gothic castle that Dracula himself would be proud of, will all be found in the new castle trail, while another castle, Ogrodzieniec, will be playable as a standalone map through Siege mode.

notes.title: The Future of Stronghold
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=sweRL93xNcA;full][/previewyoutube]
Happy New Year! After a launch that quite frankly exceeded all our expectations... We are pleased to announce that the first substantial gameplay update for [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] releases on Steam on February 13th! A simultaneous launch of free content and paid DLC, the Winter Update will be available to all players, while the [i]Swine's Bay Campaign[/i] DLC will retail for $2.99, £2.49 or €2.99.

Feeling lucky? You could even win this DLC through a giveaway being run in the above development diary! Check it out to learn more and get the inside track on what to expect of Firefly in 2024 and beyond.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44366650/4d8dda87abf2aeff2e162483401ef6a1aa1101e2.jpg[/img]

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yea-aUi9z4k]As announced before launch[/url], we intend to support [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] with both free and paid post-launch content, releasing as two major updates. The aim of each DLC is to offer fresh missions, created by veteran developers for players who want to challenge their two decades of castle sim experience. While the free updates will bring a host of fixes and improvements, alongside extra missions designed to compliment the main story.

Releasing on February 13th, the [i]Swine's Bay Campaign[/i] DLC follows the events of the main game and is narrated by returning series actor Christopher Kent. Players will be met with seven ruthless military combat scenarios across original maps, as they seek to retrieve the Jewel of the North from the clutches of the infamous slaver Captain Hogsfoot.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44366650/f992b7e75fc60c200103baeeca6b478c3228afe6.jpg[/img]

Releasing alongside this DLC, our free Winter Update will add a second economic campaign, voiced by another returning Stronghold actor in Jay Simon! These missions are designed to test players’ strategic skills beyond the warfront, with a series of resource production and management challenges. Kingdoms may be crushed by warriors, but they can only be raised by those with the vision to build.

Looking forward to the future we are actively engaged in a number of projects, the most prominent of which is the as of yet untitled ‘Stronghold Unreal’ project, built using Unreal Engine 5. Needless to say, witnessing the love for mechanically deep, passionately made strategy games like [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] has lit a fire under our little studio and the team can’t wait to share more!

In the meantime our [i]Swine's Bay Campaign[/i] is available to Wishlist, ahead of its release on February 13th:

These two updates will release early next year and arrive at the same time as one of two paid DLC military campaigns, which will each cost $2.99, £2.49 or €2.99.

Each of our two paid DLCs will release with these updates and come in the form of two new military campaigns, each offering 7 military missions. ‘Swine’s Bay’ and ‘Valley of the Wolf’ will feature the return of two popular series antagonists and lead directly on from the 14 missions included in the [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] base game. notes.title: Final Update Releasing Jan 25th
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=alFJDvQ57-I;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Update[/b]: While our big v1.10 update and Warrior Queen Campaign DLC will launch as planned on January 25th, the release of [b]Stronghold: Warlords' Ultimate Edition[/b] has now been delayed to February 14th. We apologise for this delay but hope you enjoy the free content and DLC campaign, both still releasing next week!

On Tuesday January 25th 2022 we'll be releasing our final set of Stronghold: Warlords content - A massive v1.10 update and the Fu Hao Campaign DLC, followed by a new bundle in the form of Warlords' Ultimate Edition!

Available next week v1.10 will be a free update for all owners of the game, while the Fu Hao Campaign DLC will be available to purchase alongside the upcoming Ultimate Edition, the best option for players who don't yet own Warlords and want all the DLC.

[h3][b]Fu Hao AI Opponent (v1.10)[/b][/h3]
High priestess and military general Fu Hao is our final addition to the roster of AI opponents available in Stronghold: Warlords. Mixing auxiliary class troops such as Archers and Axemen, with the heavier likes of Imperial Cavalry, Crossbowmen and Guardsmen, Fu Hao comes out swinging with a strong well-rounded army that is effective in both the early and late game.

For this legendary strategist a castle siege is about bringing siege engines with high power and rate of fire to the front line, protecting them for just long enough to punch a hole in your defences and pour her armies through before you know what happened! In order to siege Fu Hao you will need to get past eight medium towers filled with troops, along with powerful Ballistae and Mangonel platforms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/cb6087e1827d32a5a0e52b258a5d22cbbb5c2c67.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Trail of the Tyrant (v1.10)[/b][/h3]
Skirmish Trails have been a popular post-launch feature for Warlords, where many spend their time outside the main campaign and custom skirmish, so it simply wouldn’t be a final update without the addition of our longest skirmish trail yet! To that end we're adding an epic 20 mission odyssey across 12 maps, including all 8 AI lords and each of the 12 warlords available in our upcoming version 1.10.

The ‘Trail of the Tyrant’ is designed to employ every addition made to Stronghold: Warlords since launch, from new units and warlords to AI opponents and more. Some of the most beloved games in the Stronghold series are remembered for their epic-length mission trails and with the addition of Warlords’ ‘Tyrant Trail’ the game now features 45 skirmish trail missions in total.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/21508dc1af3c156e03776bcec154a791cf26b988.png[/img]

[h3][b]New Map Pack & Warlord (v1.10)[/b][/h3]
It wouldn’t be a content update without an all-new map pack and v1.10 is no different, with three unique maps bringing the total number of skirmish battleground to a whopping 28. That's in addition to 4 Free Build and 500 community maps available via Steam Workshop.

First up there’s Muddy Route - A medium sized four player map in which players will find themselves stuck fast in the deep mudflats. With little space to build your economy but plenty of open ground for fighting, this map should provide players with a challenging, but rewarding route to multiplayer victory.

Next is Windy Plains - A five player, medium sized map ideal for allied lords to face off against a rival team. This tightly-fit battleground atop the magnificent steppe, will prove challenging skirmishes for some players more than others with starting positions and resource locations acting as a handicap of sorts.

Finally we have Island Tensions - This six player map accommodates five warlords and, as the name suggests, plenty of tense combat across its land.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/38a6233904f8b41053375aaed780dedf935e9e08.png[/img]

Version 1.10 will also add a new free warlord in the form of the Lion Warlord, in addition to the release of two paid warlords (Eagle and Dog) made available as part of the Warrior Queen Campaign DLC.

A known rival to the Wolf Warlord, the Lion Warlord stands for justice above all else. Marching out to besiege his enemies with great power at his disposal, the Lion is relentless. True to his name, the Lion takes care of his pride with a perk that provides a damage boost to all infantry serving a warlord under the control of a player. As for his infantry and your choice of edicts, The Lion Warlord can provide swords, samurai and siege weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/57f6b77aaf216eb6180f1db606725586eef883fc.png[/img]

[h3][b]The Warrior Queen Campaign (DLC)[/b][/h3]
Chronicling 15 years of ancient Chinese history, The Warrior Queen Campaign brings to life a legendary commander and pivotal force in history. From counter attacks and all out assaults against the invading Tu-Fang tribe, to the Qiang Fang presence in the north and countless other adversaries, this new campaign attempts to capture the full breadth and grandeur of Fu Hao’s achievements on the battlefield.

Expect six challenging missions putting everything you’ve learnt so far to the test, including new gameplay twists such as the addition of the powerful Eagle and Dog Warlords. Step into the role of one of the most powerful and impactful military leaders history has to offer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/65631f34fa6efeb2c2c327c9aaee5ee09003c65e.png[/img]

[h3][b]What's Next?[/b][/h3]
With the January 25th release of Fu Hao, our final map pack, Lion Warlord, third skirmish trail and final DLC, followed by the Ultimate Edition on February 13th, Stronghold: Warlords will soon be content complete. We hope you’ve enjoyed playing our monthly post-release updates, get a blast out of v1.10 and look forward to the future of the Stronghold series!

The feedback we’ve received, through comments on Steam and our recent Stronghold player survey, has been invaluable in setting a course for the future of Stronghold and something we’re constantly mindful of. We’re planning to be even more open with the development of Stronghold games going forward and will be planning plenty of teaser videos and dev diaries before anything is formally revealed.

This will kick off with next month’s ‘Firefly Studios in 2022’ feature, the first of many behind the scenes videos where we confirm new and exciting information about future projects as it happens. If that sounds interesting and you'd like to learn more join us on [url=https://discord.gg/qMG7Zae]Discord[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/fireflyworlds]YouTube[/url] for the latest Stronghold news.

notes.title: Stronghold: Warlords' next AI lord is Kublai Khan, who enjoys life's finer things
notes.notes:
Medieval RTS game Stronghold: Warlords continues its glorious march through its post-launch content plans. Hot on the heels of a new patch that fixes numerous bugs (including several pesky castle wall issues), Firefly Studios has revealed its Summer and Autumn roadmap. You can expect two big updates in the next few months, and one of those will be the addition of the new AI lord Kublai Khan.

Grandson of the legendary Genghis Khan, Kublai Khan was the fifth ruler of the Mongol Empire, and lived from 1215 - 1294. In Stronghold: Warlords, Firefly says he'll behave similarly to Genghis Khan - the major difference between them being Kublai Khan's preference for expensive things. The armies he fields will be mainly built around imperial troops, and he'll demonstrate his royal privilege through his in-game taunts.

Kublai Khan will be accompanied by an all-new castle design as well as "fresh strategies to outthink and armies to outmanoeuvre," Firefly says. He'll also feature in six new missions that introduce two new warlords, and this mini-campaign will follow Kublai Khan's military exploits in China, rather than his ventures to Korea and Japan.

[list]

[b]Warlords[/b]
[list]
[*] Repair and Upgrade Castle edicts can no longer be used when the enemy is very close to the castle. If triggered before the enemy approaches, they will still finish if the enemy comes into range during the edict.

[*] Fixed several issues with turrets and engine platforms not attaching to walls correctly.

[list]
[*] The AI now takes the number of players on their team into account when choosing whether to target an enemy player or warlord, allowing them to prioritise enemy players earlier in free-for-all games.

[*] Harder AIs now better at picking Warlord Edicts and issue them more often.

[*] Defensive troops, turrets and engine platforms are now positioned more intelligently based on the direction to the closest enemy player.
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause castles not to build when spawn points are rotated.
[*] Fix for defensive troops on Genghis’ castle walls sometimes getting stuck.
[*] Tweaked the tower positions in Hideyoshi’s castle.
[*] Defensive troops now spend less time running back and forth between different positions on the walls.
[*] On Easy difficulty the AI now only builds a single layer of castle walls.
[/list]

[i]Armies[/i]
[list]
[*] The AI is now more willing to buy weapons to train troops when needed, to preserve the desired unit composition of their army.
[*] Improved the balance of Barracks and Academy troops the AI will train, whether or not they have weapons available.
[*] Fewer troops are now kept in reserve, allowing the AI to attack faster and with larger numbers when up to their troop limit.
[*] Improved the distribution of different troop types in the types of armies sent out.
[*] After capturing a warlord, armies will now sometimes guard the warlord for a period of time before moving to attack a new target.
[*] Armies that encounter an enemy keep on route to their target will now switch targets rather than continuing to their original target.
[*] Armies are better at navigating through allied estates to reach their target.
[*] Fixes for several cases where armies could get stuck while moving to their target or reforming.
[*] The AI will now more reliably start attacking with siege armies based on the number of attacks already made and their own economic development.
[*] Armies are better at tracking enemy lords who have moved away from their keeps.
[*] Fixed an issue that could stop attacks being launched once the AI reached their troop limit.
[*] Fixed several issues with the placement of forward siege camps in Warlord estates.
[*] Improved the AI’s ability to coincide Warlord attack edicts with their own attacks.
[*] Expensive troops such as Generals and Samurai are no longer held back to guard siege weapons.
[*] Fire oxen and rocket launchers no longer target warlord town buildings.
[*] Armies made up of horse archers and other cavalry now have a strong preference to tail other armies when they can, given they tend to be ineffective against enemy warlords by themselves.
[*] If individual troops in an AI army are unable to join the rest of the army for too long, they’ll now suicide in order to avoid the whole army getting stuck.
[*] Improved AI handling of rocket launchers, to avoid firing in areas that may set the ground under their own troops on fire.
[*] Genghis now sieges with more mortars and fewer rocket launchers.

[*] We have set the achievement ‘Thucing Phantastic’ to hidden for now as it is not tracking correctly. This will be addressed in a future update.

notes.title: Stronghold: Warlords is adding extreme difficulty this week, with lots more to come
notes.notes:
Building off a successful launch earlier this month, Firefly Studios has announced its plans for Stronghold: Warlords over the next several months. Between now and the end of summer, the historical RTS game will be getting a raft of new features and fixes, many suggested by the Stronghold player community.

First up is a patch coming in the next week, according to a roadmap video posted by Firefly today. In addition to several fixes and improvements, the update will also include a new extreme difficulty setting - for those among us who aren't kept sufficiently busy with building a castle, running a complex economy, and fighting a war all at the same time, this will ramp up the pressure even further.

That difficulty level will get even tougher with another future update, which is geared toward improving AI. Firefly says it plans to spruce up the AI's use of warlords, its building placement, and economic management, offering a stiffer challenge all while remaining 'cheat free.' That patch will also improve the warlords themselves with some player-requested fixes and quality of life enhancements.

Read the rest of the story...

Today we reveal the first part of our post-release content roadmap for [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b]! This first phase in our overall roadmap of updates for Warlords covers the spring and early summer period, with additional smaller patches planned and more to come in the second half of the year. Everything covered in today's announcement will be added to the game free for all players, released as soon as it's ready.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/d1ae9e3d273e5ed48e5c8fca476fa595d5149f26.jpg[/img]

Our content roadmap for [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] is divided into two separate tracks of minor or major updates. At the higher end of these 'minor updates' you'll find series staple features, such as the addition of invasions controls in Free Build mode.

notes.title: Warlords FAQ
notes.notes:
[b]Post-Launch FAQ[/b] (Last Updated September 2022)

Hi everyone,

It’s hard to believe that [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] is finally out there and in your hands! Everyone at Firefly would like to thank our community across various platforms for all the enthusiasm, valuable feedback and constructive criticism you’ve given us. It’s been a blast watching so many of you having fun building up your castles, villages and besieging friends online.  

We have put together this FAQ based on some of the feedback we’re seeing across the board. This includes some information that we have previously mentioned, but might have been missed. 

We hope you find some satisfactory answers to any issues or queries you may have. If there’s something still on your mind that you'd like to discuss, then please join us on Discord using the invite link at bottom of this post.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/e24aa07b48f3c85681ce801a87daade0c20947fa.jpg[/img]

[b]Frequently Asked Questions[/b]

[b]Will you be adding extra free content to the game?[/b]
Yes. On June 21st 2021 we released the final part of our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FYuSRk1PPaA]'Spring/Summer' content roadmap[/url] for Warlords, with our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3008949006704014083] v1.4 update[/url]. This update added the game's first skirmish trail, new maps, a brand new unit and warlords, with additional features and content added in earlier updates:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/d1ae9e3d273e5ed48e5c8fca476fa595d5149f26.jpg[/img]

Our second [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5qxWHtRquA]Summer/Autumn Roadmap[/url] was revealed on July 27th 2021, alongside the release of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/2986434179315382942]Version 1.5[/url]. The following additional content is now in game and available on Steam:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/eec455f647baa864b57d976723b29e033a621e03.jpg[/img]

Our third [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d6Sn0bQe9kA]Autumn/Winter Roadmap[/url] was revealed on November 9th 2021 and concluded with our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3121558656006439703]Version 1.10 Update[/url]. The following content is now in game and available on Steam, in addition to other minor updates such as an increased unit cap:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/d360b736a1867b7463a72427ac67be85b70fa6be.png[/img]

Our most recent (and final) release was [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3386166695433317859]Version 1.11[/url] which added a new 12 mission skirmish trail, 2 multiplayer maps and new achievements! You can learn more about the update and future plans for the series by [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gjq9bqFzsOw]clicking here[/url].

[b]Are further bug fixes, stability improvements and optimisations planned?[/b]
Fixes, improvements and optimisations will continue while we are still updating the game. Your feedback is very valuable to us and we’re focusing our energy into fixing any problems players have encountered. Beyond this feedback will be incorporated into future Stronghold titles.

[b]I am encountering bugs and/or have a technical issue.[/b]

For [b]TECHNICAL ISSUES[/b] (for example, if your game doesn't run) please contact Firefly Support by emailing support@fireflyworlds.com or going to https://support.fireflyworlds.com/

For any [b]BUGS[/b] you find (for example, unit explodes randomly) you can either follow the above or you can fill in this form by clicking on this link: 

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSffUQ8xrquINv3RS9jkqawspv1Iz2GHIDJlQMU6ZrENohCIzQ/viewform

If possible include a link to a picture or video showing the issue, as this helps us identify and resolve issues faster. Please use IMGUR (or a similar site) to upload an image or YouTube (or similar) for video. 

[b]Please Note[/b]: The more detail you provide in a bug report the more likely it is we can replicate, find and then fix it. E.g. What level of the campaign were you on? How many players/AI were involved? Did you have 70 fire oxen all explode at once? Etc.

[b]Where's my Special Edition Content?[/b]
Within Steam Client you can find the official soundtrack. You can also access all Special Edition content after installing the game, navigate to the game folder and open up a folder titled ‘Special Edition’.

By default this is located at:

C: > Program Files (x86) > Steam > steamapps > common > Stronghold Warlords > Special Edition

[b]Is mod support planned?[/b]
No mod support outside of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/907650/workshop/]Steam Workshop[/url] unfortunately, but we'll keep it in mind going forward. For now you can create custom missions, scripted events and skirmishes in the included map editor.

[b]How do I use the map editor?[/b]
Here is a guide: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2419503398 
We also have a map editor channel on our discord for people to share ideas, tips and tricks!

[b]The motion blur on the camera makes me feel sick![/b]
As of 24th March 2021, there is now a way to disable motion blur. Please refer to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3012319095278553851]V1.1 Update notes[/url] for more detail.

[b]Why did you choose Asia? I want to see more [Legends/Crusader] [/b]
Put simply, we chose Asia for its castles, battles, gunpowder and bloody, expansive history! We’re so grateful for our community’s enthusiasm for our older games set in England and the Middle East, but this time, we wanted to creatively try something different. Who knows what the future holds for us, but in the meantime we are thankful to have your support and passion! 

[b]Can I change troop/building limits in Single Player?[/b]
Warlords has been designed with specific troop and building limits in single player for gameplay and performance reasons. However we appreciate some people may wish to try playing the game with higher limits, in response to this we increased this limit just after launch in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3012319095278553851]Version 1.1[/url] and then again in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3127183081462077726]v1.9[/url].

To further alter these limits in SINGLE PLAYER:
1. Browse to the location of your Documents > Stronghold Warlords > Profiles folder.
2. Using a text editor (we recommend Notepad++) open the options.xml file.
3. On line 4 change the values for single_player_building_limit and single_player_troop_limit (make sure you retain the exact formatting used in the file).
4. Save the file.

PLEASE NOTE: These values only affect single player games not multiplayer games. Changing these values beyond the default limits may adversely affect game performance (depending on your computer).

[b]What about Multiplayer Troop/Building Limits?[/b]
As of 24th March 2021, we have increased the troop limit in skirmish mode and multiplayer. Please refer to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3012319095278553851]V1.1 Update notes[/url] for more detail.

[b][Unit/Siege weapon] is too OP! [/b]
We will be looking and managing the rebalance of units, etc with future updates and games. Please continue to give us feedback on this. 

[b]Will you continue to work on AI?[/b]
We will continue to improve AI in the game with player feedback in mind for as long as we are updating the game. This started with our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/907650/view/3012319095278553851]V1.1 Update[/url] and continued in subsequent updates, each introducing improvements to AI behaviour. Improving AI is a priority and you can expect further updates to the behaviour and challenge of opponents in future games.

[b]Is Firefly a AAA studio?[/b]
During development we had around 10 people working on Warlords, with many of us doing more than one job. We are flattered you think we might be a AAA studio, but we are very much an indie studio. Nevertheless, this did not stop us from making updates and improvements to the game post-launch.

[b]How do I access the manual for Stronghold: Warlords?[/b]
Right-click on Stronghold: Warlords in your Steam library, go to Properties, Local Files, Browse and there is a folder called Manuals.

[b]Are you working on a new Stronghold game?[/b]
Yes! We are currently in pre-production on the next entry in the Stronghold series. Check out our announcement video, Unreal 5 feature and Q&As for more:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8IEZyeK-8U

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VBTyVgTS3Nk

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fOV-nlgYeNs

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gjq9bqFzsOw

If you can think of any additional questions we can add to this FAQ, please let us know and we will add answers where possible.

Visit us on our social media:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KjLOm-zxwKI
Fans of building, besieging and ‘wuselfaktor’ rejoice! The latest entry in our almost 20 year old ‘castle sim’ series, [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] is now available on Steam. Today we celebrate the game's long awaited release with a final launch trailer featuring fresh gameplay, the full campaign map and a story preview narrated by the talented Rae Lim.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/0e9c9a350f4880b7c3e2bb1f715a53b3494098f8.jpg[/img]

Including a 31 mission campaign with conflicts and sieges ranging from 300 BC China to 16th century Japan, [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] both covers a wide historical period and (more importantly) introduces gunpowder to the series for the first time! Introducing legendary figures like Genghis Khan and lesser known rulers such as Thuc Phan, Warlords is designed to build on everything players know and love about Stronghold in an all new setting. Warlords has something for all Stronghold fans, whether you enjoy a single player campaign, unlimited castle building freedom in Free Build mode, offline skirmish or online multiplayer with friends and AI. The game comes complete with everything you expect from a mainline entry in the series, in addition to brand new gunpowder fuelled units, siege weapons and returning favourites like Siege Towers and Horse Archers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/360437ba52fd21c25c24bf0a7642ff4e92c5d52d.jpg[/img]

With [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] release we also have the introduction of the titular Warlords system, a new gameplay mechanic allowing players to conquer, upgrade and command AI ‘warlords’ across the battlefield. A flagging economy can be saved with an Ox or Pig Warlord, who can boost a players' industry and food reserves with their unique ‘Edict’ commands and passive perk abilities. Players looking to rain down fire and fury on their opponents can instead opt for a Dragon or Tiger Warlord, able to supply the player with special units and launch attacks in a pincer movement against their enemies! Whether players decide to forge these alliances through diplomatic buildings like the Consulate or simply by marching in an army and forcing warlords to bend the knee, these bonds can make or break their overall strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/51a1fd9c1e10544026ebb0bd7afb636e9df9826c.jpg[/img]

[b]Stronghold: Warlords - Special Edition[/b] is also available including Stronghold HD, ‘The Art of Stronghold: Warlords’ digital art book, a new soundtrack created by series composer Robert L. Euvino and a special ‘Making Of’ feature-length documentary.

My plan is perfect: a heavily armoured assault force of samurai and imperial swordsmen will march directly toward the gates of the enemy castle with softer reinforcements behind them, covered by wheeled mantlets. This will draw archer fire as I move my siege weapons into position. Preoccupied with the approaching menace, my opponent will not notice the ninja warriors I've directed to scale their walls. The ninjas make their way around the battlements, dispatching archers with shuriken.

Obviously, none of this works. No plan survives first contact with the enemy - or so the old military adage goes - but my plan doesn't even survive long enough to make first contact. This is Stronghold: Warlords, and part of my attacking force is caught out in the open by a cadre of speedy horse archers. Meanwhile my ninja are discovered before even reaching the walls. Compounding matters, a vassal has denied my request for a much-needed fire arrow cart as he's changed allegiances behind my back. And to top it all off, a fire has wiped out a third of my rice fields back home, sending my once-booming economy into collapse.

Warlords may have a new look and setting in feudal Asia, but long-time fans of the Stronghold series can rest assured it gives no quarter to modern notions of difficulty. This game is hard, and while its complexity is daunting, mastering its many systems might just be worth the effort.

notes.title: Why upcoming RTS Stronghold: Warlords needed to be delayed
notes.notes:
As the holiday season wrapped up, Stronghold: Warlords developer Firefly Studios faced a difficult decision: launch day was rapidly approaching, and the RTS game's multiplayer mode still wasn't performing the way it ought to. One option was to launch the single-player campaign on the scheduled release date, with the multiplayer mode to be added later.

"We were really, really considering that because we could have just released single-player, and that would have been a perfectly viable option in terms of what was actually ready at the time," marketing director Nick Tannahill says. Other games have taken this approach recently: Iron Harvest added ranked multiplayer a few weeks after launch, but saw a wave of unfavourable Steam reviews over what users saw as 'missing features' thanks to that decision.

When Firefly looked at its options, there were no hard contractual obligations that required Stronghold: Warlords to launch on the announced release date, and so the studio's leadership decided the better option was to delay launch - six weeks for the development team time to iron out the issues with multiplayer and ship the game as a complete package.

notes.title: Dev Diary - AI Improvements
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t8tZEYgdzp0 
Firefly Studios’ Designer Stephen Richards and series creator Simon Bradbury have revealed four major improvements to AI behaviour found in their upcoming ‘castle sim’ sequel Stronghold: Warlords. This new entry in the historical real-time strategy series will usher in major improvements and refinements in how computer controlled opponents interact with the player, each other and any warlords present on the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/34b9c56b7228ca35162210567781bbcf02ab4bb2.jpg[/img]

AI behaviours related to castle management, skirmish combat and city building have been completely revamped for Stronghold: Warlords, in addition to being able to work with the new warlords system. Much like the archetypes of the warlords themselves - such as the Ox, Tiger and Crane - each enemy AI will adhere to a distinct style of play over a set of predetermined behaviours. The decisions made by computer opponents will now be made according to map layout, tactical positioning of warlords, available resources, current army composition and their priorities at different stages of gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/e69633696d9779584866796cc4d3426407740b1e.jpg[/img]

In practical terms this means less hard coded, predictable behaviours and more flexibility in how AI opponents can outmanoeuvre the player, but also how it deals with the evolving situation within its own castle. Independent of the player, AI will build, sell resources and train their army according to changing priorities over the course of a skirmish match. Just as a human player would, the AI will adjust its focus between city building and RTS combat while also battling it out with the player for control over each map’s selection of warlords.

The Ninja, Warrior Monk, Imperial and Auxiliary Cavalry join the game’s roster of 16 units and 10 siege weapons accessible to all players in skirmish mode and multiplayer. Heavily reliant on remaining undetected, the Ninja is all about espionage. Able to deal high damage at range using her shuriken attack, in addition to classic invisibility and wall scaling abilities, Ninjas are more ‘hit and run’ than Assassins from previous Strongholds. When micromanaged or used in small squads, Ninjas are a force to be reckoned with. More than capable of taking out several high priority enemy units in quick succession, players will need to remain vigilant to avoid death by ninjitsu.

A well-rounded soldier with specific battlefield applications, the Warrior Monk is a finely honed living weapon. Lightly armoured and fast on his feet, this unit is capable of dealing high damage quickly and is purpose made for surprise attacks. When surrounded by three or more enemy units the Warrior Monk’s spin attack will be triggered, knocking nearby enemies out of range while also dealing damage. Their charge ability can also be used to catch enemies off balance, quickly flank them or simply charge formations head on to weaken and displace their front line.

[h3]Auxiliary Cavalry[/h3]
Faster moving than their heavily armoured Imperial counterparts, Auxiliary Cavalry are the bread and butter of a mounted attack. These faster mounted units are equipped with light armour, a shield and lance. notes.title: New Release Date: 26/01
notes.notes:
We have just announced that the release date for our upcoming RTS ‘castle sim’, [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b], has been moved from September 29 to January 26, 2021. Given the impact of COVID-19 on individual team members, this new date will result in the best possible Stronghold experience for fans of the series.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/bf7d44cabac41d1eaeb54b0bf8bf4f778f737b50.jpg[/img]

We hadn’t intended for the recent global situation to impact our development, and when we announced September 29th as our release date we fully believed we would succeed in meeting it. That said, the effect COVID-19 has had on us as individuals, as well as a company, has brought us to the point where we’ve had to take a step back, assess what areas of development still need work, and make the tough, but necessary decision to delay.

Here’s a few words on the delay from Stronghold Lead Designer, Simon Bradbury:

“Warlords is almost there and I'm loving playing it. We are currently playtesting and balancing, and there's bags of fun and challenge in there already. We are laser focused on absolutely anything that just doesn't feel right, so we need some extra time for those aspects given the current climate.

We know we can get Warlords super polished by January. We’re proud of what we have already achieved, but we feel we have to take that extra bit of time before we are happy to show it to the world. Hopefully you will stick with us as Warlords will most definitely be worth the wait.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/7bebe0e5fb7fef228fafb289e6d514ebc0abef19.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Have You Played Stronghold?
notes.notes:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time.

With Stronghold: Warlords recently announced at E3, now seems as good a moment as any to look back on the game that kicked off Firefly s seemingly endless series of castle em ups back in 2001. In fact, I m genuinely astonished to learn that Warlords will be the ninth game in the series, as despite loving the first instalment, I ve managed to play precisely none of the rest. Stronghold was a very literal tower defence game, with some light-yet-satisfying citybuilding and management elements. It also had the vague feeling of being a 14th century take on Home Alone, as you would build up your castle, then surround it with concentric layers of horrid traps in order to thwart waves of pikemen, macelads, swordboys and horseblokes.
